clue.text: Criminal visiting city in Irish county shortly

indicators.note: the pieces for visiting and city sit in the middle of the shortened county name
shortly means cut short, so the county name loses its final letter

parts.note: Clare is a county in the west of Ireland
visiting someone means being at their place
burg is an old or informal word for a town or city

explanation.surface: A news item about an offender spotted calling at some city in an Irish county.
explanation.walkthrough: Clare is a county in the west of Ireland; burg is an informal word for a city. 'Criminal' looks like an adjective but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A burglar who climbs walls to break in is a kind of criminal, so the phrase is an example of the broad term.

clue.text: Knave about right —- for one?

indicators.note: the knave word goes about, around, the right abbreviation

parts.note: a cad is a knave, a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: Is the rogue an example of right behaviour?
explanation.walkthrough: The knave is also a playing card (the jack), so the whole clue defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The knave is one of the court cards in a pack, so it is an example of the answer.

clue.text: See them in an orchestra's position raised around back of platform

indicators.note: the reversed phrase goes around the last letter of platform
in a down clue raised means the letters run upwards, reversed

parts.note: an opera orchestra sits in a pit, so it is in a pit

indicators.note: back of platform is its final letter

explanation.surface: A conductor points out where to look for them in the orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: INAPIT is turned over by 'raised' to give TIPANI, and 'around' puts M inside it. The definition gains from the rest: you see these drums in an orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: Kettledrums sit at the back of an orchestra, so you see them there; the definition is a pointer, completed by the surface.

clue.text: Secret totally gone

definitions.meaning: done covertly, as an illicit payment
gone means very drunk, so totally gone is so drunk one has slipped to the floor

explanation.surface: A confidential matter has completely vanished.
explanation.definitionFit: Covert payments are passed out of sight below the furniture, and very drunk people end up on the floor below it.

clue.text: What specifies all characteristics in system one gathers up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the hidden letters read from bottom to top
in shows the answer is inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A description of a system that collects its features together.
explanation.walkthrough: EMONEG sits in 'system one gathers' and 'up' turns it.
explanation.definitionFit: An organism's complete set of DNA encodes every inherited trait it has.

clue.text: Spring baby captivating folk of the Southern Caucasus

indicators.note: captivating means holding captive, so the folk word is held inside

parts.note: an Arian is someone born under Aries, in spring
folk, people, men

explanation.surface: A baby born in spring charms the people of a mountain region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring baby' is an astrological sign, not a newborn in April. 'folk' is in the wordplay, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Armenia lies in the southern Caucasus, so the adjective means belonging to that region.

clue.text: I do it again, getting bird

parts.note: bis is the call for a repeat performance, from the Latin for twice

explanation.surface: Someone repeats a feat and is rewarded with a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: BIS is printed in scores and shouted in theatres to ask for an encore.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-legged wading bird with a curved bill, sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Literary work not getting approved by great biographer

indicators.note: not getting means the approval word is taken out

parts.note: a book is a literary work
OK means approved
swell is informal for great or excellent

explanation.surface: A literary work fails to win the approval of a celebrated biographer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'great biographer' looks like the definition, but 'great' gives SWELL.
explanation.definitionFit: James Boswell wrote the Life of Samuel Johnson, the most famous English life story.

clue.text: Recycled waste, rubbish garment

indicators.note: recycled material is reprocessed into something new, so the letters are remade

parts.note: pants is British slang for rubbish or nonsense

explanation.surface: An item of clothing made of recycled waste is no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recycled' makes SWEAT from WASTE. Pants as slang for bad is British.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweatpants are loose trousers for exercise or lounging, a garment.

clue.text: With nothing to wreck, reversing fast

indicators.note: reversing tells us to read the pieces for nothing and wreck from end to start

parts.note: nada is Spanish for nothing, used informally in English
to mar is to spoil or wreck

explanation.surface: A driver, with nothing left to lose, backs away at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like an adverb describing the reversing, but it is the noun: a period of fasting. NADAMAR read backwards gives the month.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramadan is the Muslim month of fasting from dawn to dusk, so it is a named fast.

clue.text: Artist's partner receiving sign of affection, though not at first

indicators.note: the partner word takes the shortened affection token into its middle

parts.note: a mate is a partner or spouse

indicators.note: not at first means the opening letter is dropped from the sign of affection

parts.note: a kiss is a sign of affection

explanation.surface: A painter's partner gets a kiss, though only after some reluctance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'though not at first' reads as hesitation in the surface; it tells you to drop the opening letter of the kiss word.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was a French painter, a leading figure of Fauvism.

clue.text: Number — so make "thousand"?

parts.note: the answer read as wordplay: twist (rearrange) the two words after it, and they spell this clue word

explanation.surface: A question asking how one might produce a thousand.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: rearranging the letters of the last two words gives 'thousand'.
explanation.definitionFit: A song is a number in a musical repertoire; this one was a hit for the Isley Brothers and the Beatles.

clue.text: Hebridean island, north buried in wet earth — island for fish

parts.note: Barra is an island in the Outer Hebrides off Scotland

indicators.note: the north abbreviation is buried in the wet earth, placed inside it

parts.note: mud is wet earth
N is the compass abbreviation for north
I is a standard abbreviation for island on maps

explanation.surface: A geography of a Scottish island, with north in the mud and a fish at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: BARRA + MU(N)D + I.
explanation.definitionFit: The barramundi is a large Australasian food and game fish of the perch family.

clue.text: Amphibian scuttled off, dropping head

indicators.note: dropping head means the first letter of the word for scuttled off is lost

parts.note: someone who scuttled off has left, gone away

explanation.surface: A little creature scurried away and lost its head.
explanation.walkthrough: LEFT without its first letter gives the newt.
explanation.definitionFit: An eft is a young newt, a small tailed amphibian; the word is a crossword favourite.

clue.text: Jump aboard drunk, as damaged goods

parts.note: to hop is to jump, and aboard means within SS, the steamship abbreviation, so a jump aboard is a hop placed between two S letters
oiled is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A drunk leaps on board and ends up as damaged goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aboard' is the old convention for being in SS (steamship), so the jump sits inside those two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods soiled or faded from display in a store are sold off cheaply as damaged stock.

clue.text: Castle's home how far up?

definitions.meaning: in chess a castle or rook starts on a corner square such as h8, read out as H plus the number eight
the question asks for an altitude or vertical measurement

explanation.surface: Someone asks how high up a castle stands.
explanation.walkthrough: Chess squares are named by file letter and rank number; a rook (castle) starts on h8, said as aitch eight.
explanation.definitionFit: How far up something is, its altitude or vertical measure, is its elevation; the chess square h8 is the other reading.

clue.text: Worker in factory requiring a head scarf

indicators.note: the worker insect sits in the factory word

parts.note: a mill is a factory, such as a cotton mill
the worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A factory hand needs a headscarf for safety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worker' is the ant, not a human employee: M(ANT)ILL + A.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantilla is a lace or silk shawl worn over the hair and shoulders, especially in Spain.

clue.text: Man philosophically questioning such a load of beer?

parts.note: so can mean such, to this degree
beer is delivered in crates

explanation.surface: Wondering philosophically about whether there is so much beer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Socratic method is questioning to draw out truth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenian philosopher taught by repeated questioning, the Socratic method.

clue.text: Something in vodka I bottled unspecified number drink

indicators.note: the vegetable word holds the letter I inside it as though in a bottle

parts.note: vodka is often distilled from potatoes
n stands for an unspecified number in mathematics

explanation.surface: A vodka drinker describes the ingredient and the uncounted glasses downed.
explanation.walkthrough: POTAT(I)O + N.
explanation.definitionFit: A potation is an archaic or humorous word for an alcoholic beverage or the act of drinking.

clue.text: Outside broadcast not worth listening to?

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A disparaging verdict on an outside broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside broadcast' reads as TV; 'broadcast' scatters OUTSIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something boring and dull is not worth hearing out.

clue.text: Gallant faller at rear of pack

indicators.note: the rear of the word pack is its final letter

parts.note: night is said to fall, so it is a faller

explanation.surface: A brave rider falls at the back of the field in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faller' sounds like a horse that falls; here it is night, which falls each evening.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallant is a chivalrous man, like the armoured nobleman of romance devoted to honour.

clue.text: Starchy food providing vital energy, endless line of dancers flipping over it

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the flipped piece stands above the energy word
flipping turns the shortened dance line upside down in this down clue
endless means the last letter of the dance line is cut

parts.note: a conga is a dance in which people form a long line
chi is the vital energy in Chinese philosophy

explanation.surface: A snack fuels a conga line flipping over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts CONGA to CONG, 'flipping' turns it to GNOC, which goes 'over' CHI.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnocchi are small Italian dumplings made from potato or flour, a starchy dish.

clue.text: German physicist finds unit of acceleration down mountain

indicators.note: in a down clue the acceleration unit is placed above the mountain

parts.note: g is the unit of acceleration due to gravity
the Eiger is a mountain in the Swiss Alps

explanation.surface: A scientist discovers g-forces on a mountain descent.
explanation.walkthrough: G + EIGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Hans Geiger was the German physicist who co-invented the radiation counter named after him.

clue.text: One is this funny

definitions.meaning: the number one is not divisible by two
funny in the sense of strange or peculiar

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a person is amusing.
explanation.definitionFit: One is an uneven number, and funny can mean strange or peculiar.

clue.text: Harmony in place of high street euts?

definitions.meaning: close four-part vocal harmony style, as sung by quartets
a men's hairdresser's on a shopping street, where hair is cut

explanation.surface: A question about the effects of spending cuts on town centres.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints cuts (the text has euts from a smudge). Cuts suggests economic austerity; it means haircuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Close-harmony quartet singing takes its name from the shops where men gathered for a trim and a shave.

clue.text: Fish that's under a foot

definitions.meaning: the underside of a foot or a shoe

explanation.surface: A fish that is less than twelve inches long.
explanation.definitionFit: The underside of the foot shares its name with a flatfish, as in Dover sole.

clue.text: Ladies and gents set out, most relaxed

parts.note: the Ladies and the Gents are public toilets, informally loos

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters of set are jumbled

explanation.surface: Men and women head out, at their most easy-going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' rearranges SET as EST.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose means slack or relaxed, and the superlative form means most relaxed.

clue.text: Funny man once served crab with duck

parts.note: a crab is a bad-tempered, crabby person, a grouch
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: A comedian of old was served crab with duck at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crab' and 'duck' look like food but are a grumbler and a zero score.
explanation.definitionFit: Groucho Marx was a celebrated American comedian of the Marx Brothers, now dead, hence once.

clue.text: Dirt unfortunately spread thinly on all fronts?

definitions.text: Dirt unfortunately spread thinly on all fronts?

indicators.note: the fronts of all the words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Grime has been spread thinly everywhere, regrettably.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letters of the first four words spell the answer, and the whole clue describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine dry dirt spread in a thin layer over surfaces is a coating of powdery grime.

clue.text: Furniture item I restore, nice with edges trimmed off

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or out of order, so the letters before it are rearranged
trimming the edges of nice cuts its first and last letters, leaving the middle pair

explanation.surface: A restorer says they will do up a piece of furniture, nicely trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restore' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'off', at the very end, is the signal for I, RESTORE and IC.
explanation.definitionFit: An escritoire is a small writing desk with drawers and pigeonholes, a piece of furniture.
